messages:
anya: quick thread to capture follow-ups from the arch sync re: dedicated pool orchestration + autoscale policy. main pain: noisy gains from prewarm vs steady headroom costs. want to lock an interface for admission/decline that runtime/operator can implement.

mason: TLDR: expose clear decision enum from operator: {ADMIT, QUEUE_PREWARM, FALLBACK_VARIANT, FALLBACK_HOSTED, REJECT} plus reason codes. runtime uses that to route.

li: agree. also include fields: expected_warmup_secs, estimated_cost, idempotency_key. helps API gateway and billing.

rami: boundary question: who persists queued prewarm state? operator or control plane lease-store? if operator, control plane must poll operator for state. that makes reconciliation hairy.

devon: i'd prefer control plane persist lease intent and hand off to operator as an instruction. operator reports back status updates (IN_PROGRESS, READY, FAILED). keeps single source-of-truth.

mason: +1 to control-plane-as-SSOT. operator should be a thin executor. reduces split-brain. but operator needs a leaky-buffer cache for transient events (node boots etc.).

li: eviction/graceful drain behavior: when a pool wants to scale down we must signal runtime to start KV cache snapshot + block new long-running requests. propose a DrainPrepare notification with TTL that the runtime honors.

anya: DrainPrepare should include drain_mode: {IMMEDIATE, GRACEFUL, SLA_PREFERRED} and expected_drain_seconds. SLA_PREFERRED means prefer tenants with latency-tier to stay and evict lower-tier first.

rami: noted. autoscaler safety: when we compute headroom, we should model warmup_tail = 90s 95th percentile and include a safety multiplier (1.3). telemetry must include warmup_miss_rate.

mason: admission policy detail: allow a soft admission that returns admitted=true but path=queued (accept but not yet running). returns lease_id and a provisional token so clients can poll. return 202. make sure token is idempotent.

li: security: idempotency token must be signed HMAC by control plane key so operator can verify. prevents spurious duplicate warmups.

devon: fallback preference order: (1) variant model on same pool, (2) variant on other pool/zone, (3) shared-hosted with throttle, (4) reject with Retry-After. encode this in tenant config.

taylor: testing checklist: sim sudden 5x qps spike for mixed tenant tiers; ensure: no more than 2% requests see 503, fallback_count within expected; billing emits warmup_credit_used per lease.

mason: rollout: feature-flag runtime.admission_v2. Step 1 telemetry-only, Step 2 routing-only (no billing), Step 3 full billing + canary. default disabled.

anya: ui/contract: define response JSON for /v1/leases/grant: {admitted: "true|false", path: "dedicated|queued|variant|hosted|rejected", lease_id: "<id>" | null, eta_seconds: "int" | null, reason: "string" | null, idempotency_key: "string"}. keep fields stringy to simplify SDKs.

li: add trace_id and variant_hint fields. also add a debug field when feature-flag=telemetry-only.

rami: observability: emit events: lease_request_received, lease_decision_emitted, lease_state_transition. tag with tenant_id, pool_id, model_id, decision. dashboards: warmup_backlog_gauge, fallback_rate_by_tier.

devon: edge-case: what if operator reports READY but the node dies before runtime attaches? control plane should detect lease heartbeat missing within 10s and move to FAILED and immediately refund warmup credits.

taylor: make sure to add chaos tests (node flapping, network partition) to the ci pipeline.

mason: action items: I will draft a proto for AdmissionDecision and the HTTP contract.

li: i'll sketch metrics + prometheus labels.

rami: i'll own rollout orchestration and canary config.

anya: I'll write a short RFC follow-up that includes the playbook and the operator/control-plane boundary doc. anyone want to review?

canary-bot: scheduled canary window tentative: Wed 02:00-04:00 UTC, 0.5% tenants, golden tests: p95<120ms for latency-tier; alert if fallback_rate > 10% for >5m. :information_source:

anya: thanks all. we'll reconvene after prototypes. end.
